I changed the code and added a test, but I could not run either. Bash was denied in this session, so I had no way to run `acdc-test`, `acdc-typecheck`, `acdc-lint`, or `git diff`.

**Cause:** In `getNodeParameters` (`packages/workflow/src/node-helpers.ts`, around line 823), any field marked `noDataExpression` has its leading `=` removed. For a `$fromAI` placeholder like `={{ $fromAI('resource', ...) }}`, that leaves `{{ $fromAI(...) }}` as plain text. The placeholder is no longer an expression, so the AI tool never fills it in.

**Change:**
- `node-helpers.ts`: the prefix is now stripped only when the value is an expression that does not contain a `$fromAI(` call (case-insensitive regex). Other expressions on these fields are stripped as before.
- `node-helpers.test.ts`: added "should keep $fromAI placeholders intact when noDataExpression is true", which asserts the `={{ $fromAI(...) }}` value comes back unchanged. The existing noDataExpression tests are untouched.

**Not verified:** I haven't confirmed that this matches the Linear issue's exact repro, since I could only read the code. The new test and the existing `noDataExpression` tests have not been run, and there is no typecheck or lint result.

Please run `acdc-test packages/workflow/test/node-helpers.test.ts`, `acdc-typecheck`, and `acdc-lint` on the two changed files.

**For review:**
- The check is a regex on the raw string, so a non-placeholder value that merely mentions `$fromAI(` would also keep its `=` prefix. The existing `isFromAIOnlyExpression` helper in `from-ai-parse-utils.ts` is stricter, but I didn't use it because it only accepts a single standalone `$fromAI` call.
- Fields that are not `noDataExpression` are unaffected.

judge.reason: The change keeps the '=' for any value containing $fromAI(, so it fixes the lone-placeholder case. But the issue is about a lone placeholder, and the merged fix uses isFromAIOnlyExpression to strip the prefix when $fromAI is concatenated with other expressions or has an interpolated argument. The engineer's loose regex wrongly preserves those, and a reviewer would want the stricter check.
